prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create one transparent top-down RTS game asset: Early Medieval Russian/Rus overland fur trader. Reference is PRIMARY camera, painted sprite quality, anatomy and assembly reference; simplify it to exactly ONE merchant, ONE pulling horse, ONE two-wheel cart, NO pack animal or second merchant. Entire assembly travels toward SCREEN BOTTOM. Strict90degree vertical overhead orthographic, seen from directly above, no horizon, no isometric side view. Cart in upper center/right, chestnut horse directly below cart between two connected wooden shafts, merchant walking alongside horse on screenLEFT holding a short curved lead rein connected to horse bridle. Horse is anatomically compact with 4short believable legs mostly occluded from directly above, no elongated front limbs, no splayed sticks. Empty space around merchant and horse permits walking animation. Cart is wooden with exactlytwo narrow round wooden wheels seen edge-on from above, plain smooth iron rims, no blocks or bumps in tread. Cargo reads immediately: two bound brown fur rolls, one cream linen bale, one small timber chest, rope tied securely across cart floor; no guns or militarygear. Merchant wears muted mossgreen wool tunic, brown belt pouch, rust-red woven sash, small rounded darkfur cap, plain trousers/leather boots, medievalregionalRus materials rather than soldier armor; shoulders and capTOP dominant, no frontal portrait. Maintain strongly legible connected horse-cart silhouette. Reference retains only one leftmerchant+mainhorse+cart arrangement; remove all right-side members. Center the complete group on square canvas, >=80px genuinely transparent guard on ALL edges, no clipping. Same crisp dimensional painted gameart style, subduedearthpalette, clear cargo/readability at48/64/128px. Genuine RGBA transparency, no ground, no shadows outside assembly, no text/glow/atlas. One static source master only; proportions mechanically coherent, reins/harness/shafts attached.
historicalScope: Rus-inspired regional game interpretation, not a specific archaeological reconstruction.
